results.market_title: Will Swedish Social Democratic Party (S) win at least 33% of all valid votes?
results.reasoning: Recent August 2026 polls (Demoskop, PolitPro average) show the Social Democrats polling around 30-31%, having drifted down slightly from a higher of ~32% seen in May 2026 Ipsos poll. To reach the 33% threshold by election day (Sep 13, 2026) would require an upward swing of 2-3 points from current trend, which is plausible but not the base case given the party has consistently polled in the 30-31% range for months.

results.market_title: Will the highest temperature in Milan be 23°C on September 17?
results.reasoning: Multiple forecast sources (AccuWeather, Ventusky) for Milan/Linate around Sept 17, 2026 point to a high temperature near 26-27°C (79-81°F), somewhat above the September climatological average of ~24-25°C for the region. Malpensa airport, being further from the city and at slightly higher elevation, often runs a degree or two cooler than central Milan/Linate readings, but even accounting for that the most likely bracket appears to be 24-26°C rather than exactly 23°C. Given several days of lead time, forecast uncertainty remains, but current data leans against the 23°C bracket being the outcome.
results.key_findings: ["AccuWeather forecast for Milan (city center) shows Sept 17 high of ~81°F (~27°C)","Ventusky forecast for Milano/Linate shows Sept 17 high of ~79°F (~26°C)","September average high in Milan is typically around 24-25°C (77°F), so current forecasts trend slightly warmer than average","Malpensa airport typically reads a bit cooler than central Milan due to distance/elevation, but not usually by 3-4°C"]

results.market_title: Will the highest temperature in Milan be 22°C on September 17?
results.reasoning: AccuWeather's Milan (city) forecast for Sept 17, 2026 shows a high near 81°F (~27°C), well above the 22°C bracket, though a duplicate/mislabeled Milan entry suggested a cooler ~22°C day, indicating some forecast uncertainty at 2-day lead time. Malpensa airport (outside the city, slightly higher elevation) often runs 1-3°C cooler than downtown Milan readings, but even accounting for that the most probable high still lands in the mid-to-upper 20s°C rather than exactly 22°C.
results.key_findings: ["AccuWeather Milan city forecast (station 214046) shows Sept 17 high of 81°F (~27°C)","A separate/duplicate AccuWeather Milan listing showed 71°F (~22°C) for the same date, indicating conflicting forecast sources","Malpensa airport readings are typically a few degrees cooler than central Milan due to location/elevation","Two-day-out forecasts still carry meaningful uncertainty, but most sources point to a warmer (mid-to-high 20s°C) outcome than exactly 22°C"]

results.market_title: Will the Sweden Democrats (SD) win the third most seats in the 2026 Swedish parliamentary election?
results.reasoning: Multiple independent polling aggregators (PolitPro, Ipsos, Polara) consistently show Sverigedemokraterna (SD) polling around 19-20%, ahead of Moderaterna at roughly 17.5-18%, giving SD a fairly stable ~1.5-2.5 point lead and translating to seat projections of roughly SD 70 seats vs. M 65-69 seats. This gap has persisted across many polls and pollsters over recent months, making SD landing in second place (not third) the clear base case, mirroring the 2022 election outcome where SD also finished second ahead of M. For SD to fall to third, M would need to close and overtake a multi-point, multi-pollster gap in the final weeks — possible but not the current trend, so I estimate the probability of SD finishing third at around 15%, below the market's 33% crowd price.
results.key_findings: ["PolitPro Election Trend (Aug 28, 2026): S 30.7%, SD 19.2%, M 17.9% — SD projected 70 seats vs M 65 seats","Ipsos poll (May 2026): SD 20% vs M 19%, SD projected 73 seats vs M 69 seats","Polara aggregator (late Aug 2026): SD 19.6% vs M 17.5%, consistent SD lead over M","2022 election precedent: SD finished second nationally ahead of M, matching the current polling pattern","In 2022 SD already outpolled M, so a reversal in 2026 would require a notable swing in the final stretch before the Sep 13 2026 for M to overtake SD"]

results.market_title: Will the highest temperature in Toronto be 23°C on September 16?
results.reasoning: Environment Canada's official forecast (issued Sept 14, valid for Sept 16 at Toronto Pearson) calls for a high of 26°C with cloudy periods/showers, and other aggregators corroborate a high in the mid-to-upper 20s°C range. Since the forecast mean (~25-26°C) sits noticeably above the 23°C bracket, and short-range forecast uncertainty (±1.5-2°C) means the exact-degree bucket of 23°C is a tail outcome rather than the central estimate.
results.key_findings: ["Environment Canada 7-day forecast (issued ~Sept 14, 2026) lists Wed Sept 16 high as 26°C with 'A mix of sun and cloud' at Toronto Pearson","A secondary aggregator (weatherin.org) independently shows a high of ~78°F (25.6°C) for Sept 16 in Toronto, consistent with Env Canada","Climatological normal high for mid-September in Toronto is ~21-22°C, but the specific 2026 forecast is running warmer than normal for this date","No source found forecasting a high near 23°C specifically for Sept 16, 2026"]

results.market_title: Will the Fed increase interest rates by 25 bps after the September 2026 meeting?
results.reasoning: The Fed is in an unusual mid-cycle debate between renewed hawkish inflation/energy pressure and a weakening labor market. Live prediction markets (Kalshi, ~$16M volume) as of late August 2026 price a 25bp September hike at roughly 30-31%, implying ~69-70% for 'no change,' and weak July/August jobs data (per Motley Fool, Aug 12) has caused hike odds to 'plunge' from earlier July highs near 50%+. Wall Street desks are split (Goldman calling a hike 'very unlikely,' JPMorgan flagging a hike as newly plausible amid energy shocks), but the most recent, highest-liquidity market signal leans toward a hold rather than a hike.
results.key_findings: ["Kalshi's live Sept 2026 FOMC market prices Hike 25bps at ~31% (No 70%) as of late August 2026","DeFiRate aggregation of Kalshi/Polymarket shows 67.9% probability of holding steady, 30.5% for a 25bp hike after Aug 19 FOMC minutes","Motley Fool (Aug 12, 2026): 'odds of a September rate hike have plunged' after a weak jobs report, despite hawkish tilt at July meeting (3 dissents favoring a hike)","MUFG Research (Aug 2026) expects Fed to stay on hold through 2026, seeing 30-60% hike probability priced per meeting but doubting urgency to hike","Current target range is 3.50%-3.75% under new Chair Kevin Warsh, unchanged for five consecutive meetings through July 2026"]

results.market_title: Will the Fed increase interest rates by 25 bps after the September 2026 meeting?
results.reasoning: Multiple contemporaneous sources (Chase, Marketplace, CBS News, centralbank.watch) converge on a shift toward a 25bp hike at the September 15-16, 2026 FOMC meeting, driven by persistent inflation concerns and energy price shocks tied to the Iran conflict, with Fed Chair Warsh publicly noting inflation 'hasn't meaningfully improved.' Market-implied probability from centralbank.watch was around 66%, close to the crowd price of 80%, and this represents a notable reversal from the Fed's 2025 easing cycle (three consecutive cuts) and earlier 2026 expectations of continued cuts.
results.key_findings: ["Chase: '25-Basis-Point Move Is Now Expected' for September 2026, a shift from prior no-change base case","Marketplace.org: 'Fed watchers expect the FOMC to raise rates at its September meeting' after Warsh's inflation comments","centralbank.watch: market-implied probability of a 25bp hike at ~66% for the Sept 16, 2026 meeting","CBS News: September FOMC could be 'first meaningful test' of hike odds amid Iran-related supply shocks","Prior to this shift, Fed had cut rates three times in 2025 (Sept, Oct, Dec) to 3.5%-3.75%, and Goldman Sachs still projected further 2026 cuts as base case"]

results.market_title: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the September 2026 meeting?
results.reasoning: This is an unusual environment: under new hawkish Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, sticky inflation (~3.4% CPI, hot core readings) and strong payrolls have shifted prediction markets and futures decisively toward a 25bp HIKE rather than a hold at the Sept 15-16, 2026 FOMC meeting. Multiple recent (within days) sources (Polymarket, Kalshi, futures) show hike probabilities ranging 58-70%, up sharply from ~25% just weeks earlier after Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks, implying 'no change' is now the less likely outcome.
